title: Resonance crossings and diabolical points for DC electric field quantum sensors
abstract: Since the 1990s, experiments on double-well heterostructures have highlighted a key phenomenon: applying an external DC electric field induces pronounced wave packet oscillations at specific field strengths. \ To gain a deeper insight into this effect, a comprehensive quantitative analysis of the properties of quantum resonances near a crossing point is required. \ This approach lays the theoretical foundation for devising a quantum sensor capable of rapidly and efficiently determining whether the strength of an external DC electric field lies within a narrow target range.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical model for using quantum resonances in double-well heterostructures as a highly sensitive electric field sensor. By analyzing the phenomenon of resonance crossings (specifically Type I), the authors show that large-amplitude quantum beating oscillations occur precisely at a critical electric field strength. This provides a pathway for engineering solid-state quantum devices for precise field measurement.
main_problem: To develop a theoretical foundation for a quantum sensor capable of rapidly and efficiently determining if an external DC electric field strength lies within a narrow target range.
main_result: The theoretical framework predicts that achieving a single Type I resonance crossing (RC) allows for a highly sensitive quantum sensing scheme for measuring the DC electric field strength.
method: The analysis involves solving the time-independent Schrödinger equation for a double-well potential under an external field, utilizing Airy's special functions and complex scaling methods.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a double-well heterostructure (e.g., GaAs/AlGaAs) whose quantum resonances are perturbed by an external DC electric field (F). The Hamiltonian is parameterized by F.
key_observables: The existence and type of resonance crossings (RCs), the beating dynamics of the wavefunction (survival amplitude $A(t)$), and the expansion coefficients $|C_{Ej}|^2$.
important_parameters: The DC electric field strength (F), and structural parameters like well widths ($\ell_{w1}, \ell_{w2}$) and barrier widths ($\ell_{b1}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on treating the system as a non-symmetric $2 	imes 2$ matrix near the crossing point, and the use of BenDaniel and Duke matching conditions.
figures_summary: Figure 2 shows avoided crossings of resonance real parts and $|C_{Ej}|^2$ vs. F. Figure 3 shows the narrow Type I RC for optimized parameters. Figure 4 illustrates the resulting large-amplitude oscillations of the survival amplitude $A(t)$ near the crossing point.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem (quantum sensing via resonance crossings), develops the mathematical framework using the Schrödinger equation and special functions, analyzes the resonance crossing types (Type I/II), and concludes by demonstrating the sensor principle using optimized parameters.
why_interesting: This work directly applies advanced quantum mechanical techniques (resonance analysis, complex scaling) to a solid-state platform for sensing, bridging fundamental quantum theory with practical device physics.

Within the envelope-function approximation, the potential V (x) corresponds to a tilted double square well with no bound states, supporting instead the quantum resonances E1 (solid line) and E2 (dashed line).

Figure 2. Left-hand panel: avoided crossings of the real parts of the four resonances E1 (solid line), E2 (dashed line), E3 (dotted line), and E4 (dash-dotted line), showing three Type I RCs at F = 7.9(6) kV/cm, F ≈30 kV/cm, and F ≈65 kV/cm. Right- hand panel: squared absolute values |CEj|2 (j = 1, 2, 3, 4) of the expansion coefficients in formula (6). The model parameters are taken from [8].

Figure 3. Left-hand panel: avoided crossing of the real parts of the two resonances E1 (solid line) and E2 (dashed line). Right- hand panel: crossing of the imaginary parts of the two resonances. The RC is of Type I and occurs at F = FC = 13.087(5) kV/cm, with heterostructure parameters given by (7).

Figure 4. The squared absolute values of the coefficients CE1 (solid line) and CE2 (dashed line) (left-hand panel) and the abso- lute value of A(t) for an initial wavefunction localized in just one well (right-hand panel), for model parameters given by (7). A complete beating motion occurs for F = FC (solid line), whereas no large-amplitude oscillations appear for F = FC · 1.01 (dashed line).
